Regeneration without a recruitment cap

Source: R/Processes.R
regeneration.Rd

FINN's uncapped mechanistic regeneration process: the mean number of recruits a species contributes to one patch in one simulation step, in stems per hectare, mean = regP * exp(pred) + reg_floor. regP is the patch's light response, a sigmoid in the available light centred on the species' light requirement parReg and shifted to be 0 without light, so a shade-tolerant species (small parReg) recruits under a closed canopy and a light-demanding one does not. exp(pred) is the species' environmental response, and reg_floor (createProcess(), default 1e-3) is an additive floor that keeps a species from being lost for good.

The mean is unbounded in pred, so a steep climate coefficient can turn a favourable site into a recruitment burst of hundreds of stems in one year. regeneration_capped() adds a Beverton-Holt cap and is the default regeneration process since 0.2.0; this function is the uncapped process of Pichler & Käber (2026) and stays available as the opt-in.

Usage

regeneration(species, parReg, pred, light, debug = FALSE)

Arguments

species

torch.Tensor species information.

parReg

torch.Tensor Regeneration parameters. 0 <= parReg <= 1 This parameter denotes the fraction of light needed for a species to regenerate. In general low values for high regeneration and high values for low regeneration.

pred

torch.Tensor Prediction values.

light

torch.Tensor Available light variable for calculation.

debug

logical If TRUE, return the intermediate components as a list. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

torch.Tensor Mean recruitment per species, stems ha^-1 step^-1, shaped [sites, patches, species] – a per-HECTARE rate, not a per-patch count: forward() multiplies it by patch_size_ha itself before the recruit draw. It includes the additive reg_floor and is unbounded above.

See also

regeneration_capped() (the default regeneration process since 0.2.0), regeneration_adult(), recruitment for the recruitment options and how to combine them

Examples

# the uncapped regeneration of the paper instead of the default
# regeneration_capped(); recruits enter at 1 cm (recruits_dbh)
m <- finn(N_species = 2, recruits_dbh = 1,
          regeneration_process = createProcess(~ 1 + temp, regeneration))

# a 30-year simulation from bare ground; an unfitted model uses `env` as
# given (no scaling constants yet), so the predictor is passed standardised
env <- data.frame(siteID = 1L, year = 1:30, temp = 0)
sim <- simulateForest(m, env = env, patches = 5, patch_size = 0.1)
tail(sim$wide$site)
